597090.new:
Hands-on Lab: Spot the group

Tap any atom of the named group in a real molecule: a drug, a flavor or an amino acid. A right tap lights up the whole group; a wrong tap tells you which group that atom belongs to. This set asks only about groups you know so far: alcohol, phenol, ether, thiol, and the alkene from Chapter 3. Your progress is saved in this browser.

Hands-on Lab: Build and break fats

Build a triacylglycerol one ester bond at a time by tapping the –OH of a fatty acid and the H of glycerol that leave as water, then take fats and waxes apart by hydrolysis (acid or lipase) or saponification (NaOH or KOH). A wrong pick tells you why it is wrong. Your progress is saved in this browser.

597168.new:
Hands-on Lab: Enzyme Bench

Every control is live: amount of substrate, amount of enzyme, temperature, pH, and the enzyme itself (pepsin, trypsin or a typical body enzyme). The red dot shows the rate at your settings. Work through the goals, such as finding where more substrate stops helping, or denaturing the enzyme with heat and cooling it again. The inhibitor controls belong to Section 11.4. For guided questions (predict, change one control, explain), open the Enzyme Bench lab.

597169.old: Drugs that are inhibitors
597169.new:
Hands-on Lab: Inhibitors on the Enzyme Bench

An inhibitor is present and the substrate is low. Predict what flooding the enzyme with substrate will do, turn the substrate up, then explain the result and apply it to a new case. A competitive inhibitor can be outcompeted by more substrate; a noncompetitive inhibitor cannot. Your progress is saved in this browser.
